items.title: PhD Measuring and Scaling Agentic Software Engineering (f/m/x)
items.desc:
THE FUTURE IS WHAT WE CREATE WHEN WE TAKE OUR VISIONS TO THE LIMITS. 
 PHD AT THE BMW GROUP. 
 Bridging the gap between your doctoral studies and the kind of career challenge you’re looking for isn’t always easy. That’s why our ProMotion PhD programme gives you the opportunity to apply your passion and scientific expertise to very real challenges that could shape the future of mobility. If selected, you’ll have the chance to really develop your own future career path with us through your practice-related thesis, promote your chosen specialty from within – and position yourself to secure the career you’ve always wanted.
 Our New Technologies team explores and evaluates emerging technologies and brings the most promising ones into productive use across the BMW Group. Agentic software engineering is one of these technologies, and as a PhD candidate, you help find ways to systematically measure agentic software development and scale it to real-world use. 
 What awaits you? 
 You design benchmarks that evaluate coding agents on real automotive codebases across the full development lifecycle. 
 Within this project, you investigate where agents lose relevant code between exploration and generation - a failure mode that grows with codebase size and remains unmeasured. 
 Building on these insights, you explore methods that help agents preserve and use relevant code more effectively. 
 In this role, you help develop verification and testing approaches that keep agent-generated code trustworthy without slowing down development. 
 Together with the team, you benchmark agent configurations, LLMs, harnesses and scaffolding across heterogeneous stacks such as embedded C/C++, Java, Python and Go. 
 Finally, you translate your findings into research and deployment frameworks that can be applied at real-world scale. 
 What should you bring along? 
 Studies in computer science, data science, mathematics or a comparable field. 
 Solid knowledge of machine learning, in particular large language models and agentic systems. 
 Strong programming skills in Python; experience with C/C++, Java or Go is an advantage. 
 Hands-on experience with agent evaluation and benchmarking, for example SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, tau-bench or comparable frameworks. 
 Ideally first publications or submissions at relevant scientific venues during your studies. 
 Very good English language skills; German is an advantage.

items.desc: PhD fellowship in climate and health epidemiology A 3-year PhD fellowship is available at the Work, Environment and Cancer group at the Danish Cancer Institute. The position We are seeking a PhD student to work on a large EU-funded consortium project, Understanding and Preventing Climate-Related Health Risks through Mediating Pathways (U-PATH) . Europe is the fastest-warming continent, yet evidence that separates direct heat effects from effects mediated by other environmental exposures, such as air pollution, aeroallergens, noise, and indoor overheating, is still lacking. U-PATH brings together 15 international research institutions to investigate how climate exposures relate to cardiovascular and respiratory disease, with a particular focus on the mediating role of environmental exposures. The Work, Environment and Cancer group’s main tasks in U-PATH include: coordinating the harmonization of epidemiological data from cohorts in five countries contributing data and analyses from a Danish nationwide cohort conducting measurement campaigns of indoor summer temperatures, which will be used to develop a model for indoor heat exposure assessment coordinating analyses of associations between long-term residential indoor and outdoor heat events and risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease across the cohorts The Work, Environment and Cancer research group is a dynamic multi-national team of researchers dedicated to studying the effects of environmental and occupational exposures on the development of cancer and other diseases. Your main responsibilities Conduct indoor temperature measurement campaigns Contribute to developing a model for indoor exposure assessment Link climate exposure data to Danish residential addresses Generate analysis-ready datasets with climate and environmental exposures, health outcomes, and potential confounders for the Danish population Analyze associations between climate and environmental exposures and risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease, in collaboration with key U-PATH partners Write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals Present results at U-PATH consortium meetings and international conferences PhD enrolment You will be enrolled as a PhD student at a Danish university and supervised by researchers from the Work, Environment and Cancer group. Enrolment is subject to approval by the relevant PhD school, and it is a prerequisite for receiving the stipend that you are enrolled as a PhD student. Your progress as a PhD student will be assessed at regular intervals. As part of your PhD studies, you will be required, among other things, to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS and to undertake a research stay of 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. Qualifications Required A master’s degree (completed or nearly completed) in public health, epidemiology, statistics, or related discipline Experience in statistical programming, preferably in SAS and/or R A systematic and well-organized work approach, with strong planning and collaboration skills Excellent written and spoken English An advantage Experience with statistical analyses in quantitative epidemiological research Experience with large datasets and register-based data Experience with GIS software, such as QGIS Experience with contributing to peer-reviewed publications Interest in or experience with field data collection We offer An inspiring and dynamic working environment in an interdisciplinary research center (biologists, human biologists, public health scientists, medical doctors, data managers, psychologists, statisticians, etc.) where we work with many different epidemiological and biological topics. The research department regularly hosts interdisciplinary seminars with external lecturers on biological and epidemiological research areas and internal courses on relevant topics. Also, we have a Postdoc network that arranges regular meetings and seminars. Salary, pension, and conditions of employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish government and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). We offer canteen, fruit scheme, sports- and art clubs as well as physiotherapy. You will initially be employed as research assistants to allow time for enrollment as PhD students at the University. You are expected to write your PhD application with support from your supervisor. The Danish Cancer Society of course has a no smoking policy during working hours. Start date: The position is a 3-year full-time position and is open from January 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. More information For specific information about the project or the position, please contact Group Leader and Professor Mette Sørensen, mettes@cancer.dk, +45 3525 7626 Application and deadline Submit your application no later than 15th of November 2026 . Applications submitted after this date will not be considered. We only accept applications through our electronic system at www.cancer.dk/job. The application must include: A cover letter (maximum two pages) describing how your qualifications match the project A detailed CV A Master's degree diploma, or documentation of expected completion A list of publications, if any, including submitted manuscripts Application due 11/15/2026 Start date 1/1/2027 Work hours Position category Position type Workplace Copenhagen Homepage https://www.cancer.dk Contact Mette Sørensen Gruppeleder 35257626 More vacant positions Follow us

items.title: PHD POSITION IN URBAN SOCIAL RESILIENCE WITHIN SUSTAINABILITY AND PLANNING
items.desc: Description of the Position Aalborg University invites applications for a PhD position in Sustainability and Planning Research focusing on urban resilience from a systemic and planning-oriented perspective. The PhD project explores the dynamic relationships between people, places, and material environments and is situated within an emerging research agenda investigating how design thinking and planning practices can support circularity and sustainability initiatives in cities. This PhD position, funded by the project “Co-creating regenerative green-social infrastructures for urban circular economies” ( WeGrowCircle ) through the Driving Urban Transitions Partnership, is part of a new interdisciplinary thematic research initiative addressing Urban Social Resilience (USR) with particular attention to care ethics, participatory processes, and social innovation as guiding perspectives. The successful candidate will contribute to interdisciplinary research activities, empirical studies, and scholarly publications in close collaboration with other members of the USR initiative across the Department of Sustainability & Planning and the Department of Architecture, Design & Media Technology. The position further offers engagement in a wider research network spanning urban sustainability, innovation, planning, design, and architecture. The position is available from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter, and with employment in the Sustainability, Innovation and Policy research group. The duration of the position is three years. Research Focus The PhD project addresses the pressing challenge of developing urban social resilience in cities, with a particular focus on how social actors, relations, and practices can gain agency in resilience-building processes through inclusive, collaborative, participatory, and planning-based approaches across actors, organisations, and institutions. The project is grounded in a socio-material planning and design perspective, where urban resilience is understood as an emergent quality produced through interactions between social dynamics, institutional frameworks, and material and spatial configurations. Within this framework, the PhD project must in particular contribute to: establishing a shared conceptual and methodological foundation for the WeGrowCircle project, e.g. as a Resilient Urban Commons Framework mapping and analysing actor landscapes, relations, and key dynamics in the development of urban social resilience and regenerative green-social infrastructures (GSIs) developing and testing an inclusive co-creation process for GSI design, exploring stewardship and governance models for resilient and collective land management, evaluating how GSIs can improve biodiversity, circular practices, sufficiency, and social well-being; and generating evidence and recommendations for integrating GSIs into local planning, climate action and community practice. The PhD project may adopt different disciplinary perspectives, empirical focus areas, and methodological approaches within the broader field of urban social resilience and planning. At the same time, it is expected that the project will relate to and further develop the research environment’s work with socio-material approaches, participatory and interactive planning, as well as co-design and co-production in the context of urban resilience. Applicants are therefore expected to develop and outline a preliminary research proposal (1–3 pages) that presents their initial considerations regarding research focus, research design, and methodological approach in relation to urban social resilience within a planning and design perspective. Research Context The specific empirical context of the PhD project is closely linked to the WeGrowCircle project and thus mainly to the Aalborg Living Lab. However, engagement with one or more of the other three living labs (Brussels, Gothenburg, Bucharest) in the project is expected. Decision about which one(s) is intentionally left open at this point, and need not be considered in the application. Your Competences Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in exploring how urban resilience is shaped through the interplay between social and material dimensions. The PhD project is expected to investigate planning and design processes with particular attention to participatory, co-design, and co-production approaches, as well as the use of mapping as an analytical and generative research method. Applicants must hold a Master’s degree in sustainability and planning, urban studies, sustainability and design, geography, or a related discipline. Experience with qualitative, participatory, and design-oriented research methods—including co-design or co-production—is considered a significant advantage. The ideal candidate is motivated to work in interdisciplinary research environments and is interested in collaborating across disciplines and with a wide range of urban stakeholders, including planners, designers, and public sector actors. The candidate should demonstrate curiosity, independence, and initiative, and be motivated to develop and conduct a PhD project involving co-design and co-production in close collaboration with supervisors and research partners. Qualification requirements PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. What we Offer The position offers a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment rooted in contemporary sustainability and planning research. The PhD candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to and shape a growing body of research on design and planning for urban social resilience. The position includes support for scholarly publications and public communication of research, and carries an obligation for teaching, supervising, and involvement in the Department’s bachelor and master programmes on planning and sustainability. How to apply Your application must include the following: Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position Curriculum Vitae (CV) Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) A preliminary research proposal (1–3 pages) Other relevant documents The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. Do you have any questions? You may obtain further information from Associate Professor Martin Lehmann martinl@plan.aau.dk concerning the scientific aspects of the stipend. For further information about stipends and salary as well as practical issues concerning the application procedure contact Lisbeth Diinhoff, The Doctoral School at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design, email: ld@adm.aau.dk Further information Read more about our recruitment process here. The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts. Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not. The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. Read more about The Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design Salary and terms of employment The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”. There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen. items.title: THESE EN INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE (H/F)
items.desc: 35170 Bruz, Bretagne CDD A propos de Sogitec Venez faire décoller vos talents à nos côtés ! Société d’ingénierie en aéronautique, SOGITEC est leader dans la conception, le développement, la production et la fourniture de produits et services de simulation, pour la formation et l’entrainement au sol des pilotes et mécaniciens qui emploient et soutiennent les aéronefs réels. Filiale à 100% de Dassault Aviation, l’entreprise compte plus de 300 collaborateurs et s’impose comme un partenaire de premier niveau au service des constructeurs aéronautiques. Combinant sa longue expérience des exigences opérationnelles et ses compétences dans l’intégration des nouvelles technologies, telles que l’intelligence artificielle ou la réalité virtuelle, SOGITEC investit dans la recherche et l’innovation. Ainsi, SOGITEC intervient en tant que maître d'œuvre de programmes français et internationaux, complexes, pluriannuels et impliquant de multiples coopérations industrielles. SOGITEC s’appuie sur un socle d’affaires en forte consolidation grâce aux ventes du RAFALE et de ses moyens de simulation, dont il est le fournisseur exclusif. De plus, SOGITEC s’adapte aux besoins d’entraînement des Forces aériennes pour les derniers hélicoptères d’AIRBUS Helicopter par la fourniture des simulateurs de NH90 et prochainement du tout nouveau HIL (H160M). Enfin, SOGITEC développe de nouveaux produits de simulation dans les domaines des drones et des hélicoptères, y compris pour le personnel dédié à l’emploi du treuil et de l’armement. Ces succès reposent sur des équipes passionnées et dynamiques, d’un très haut niveau d’expertise technique, sur l’envie de repousser les limites et la capacité à faire face aux exigences d’une activité en constante évolution pour construire l’avenir. Votre mission THESE EN INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE : CONTRÔLE PAR INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE DES ENTITÉS VIRTUELLES D’UN SIMULATEUR DE VOL AFIN D’ATTEINDRE LES OBJECTIFS DE LEUR MISSION. A SOGITEC, VOUS SEREZ : Dans le cadre de ses activités de simulation d’avions d’armes et d’hélicoptères, SOGITEC souhaite renforcer sa capacité à modéliser et à simuler le comportement des forces en présence à partir de techniques d’intelligence artificielle. Les simulateurs développés par ses équipes s’appuient sur un serveur tactique pour animer les entités aériennes, terrestres et navales présentes sur le théâtre d’opérations virtuel. Pour un opérateur ou un moniteur simulation, paramétrer chacune de ces entités requiert un travail fastidieux pour obtenir le résultat souhaité en termes de déplacement ou réaction. Depuis plusieurs années, SOGITEC investigue des méthodes d’apprentissage machine afin d’envisager un contrôle plus intuitif des entités programmables. Les algorithmes employés ont jusqu’ici produit des résultats prometteurs mais l’entreprise souhaite poursuivre ses travaux de recherche afin d’identifier des solutions flexibles capables de gérer des situations plus complexes (grand nombre d’entités, diversité des missions/situations, etc). Dans ce contexte SOGITEC et ISAE-SUPAERO souhaitent travailler en collaboration, au travers d’une thèse CIFRE, pour lever les verrous technologiques correspondants :  Recenser les missions d’intérêt, identifier le meilleur moyen de modéliser ces missions et de les paramétrer par un utilisateur.  Identifier l’architecture algorithmique de contrôle des entités qui doit en résulter.  Statuer sur le niveau de contrôle.  Évaluer la scalabilité/portabilité de la solution. Votre profil AUJOURD’HUI VOUS ÊTES : Vous devez disposer d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 avec un M2 recherche ou avec une expérience avérée de recherche (obligatoire). Cadre de travail : Vous serez rattaché(e) à la Direction des Simulations à SOGITEC, et serez sous la responsabilité de son chef de service. En tant que doctorant(e) spécialisé(e) dans l’IA, vous devez être en capacité d’imaginer de nouvelles solutions dans ce domaine, adaptées à nos problématiques. Vous serez également inscrit(e) à l’ISAE-SUPAERO, Université de Toulouse, qui sera votre laboratoire d’accueil doctoral. Vous serez rattaché(e) au département DCAS, sous la supervision de ses directeurs de thèse. Vous participerez également à des projets stratégiques intégrant (non exhaustif) le Deep Learning avancé, Apprentissage par Renforcement (RL) ou encore l’IA générative et modèles de langage (LLM), et serez en en étroite collaboration avec les équipes techniques et métiers afin de transformer les besoins fonctionnels en solutions algorithmiques performantes et industrialisables chez SOGITEC. Dans ce cadre, vous réaliserez des travaux d'études bibliographiques, d'études algorithmiques, de prototypage, de développement logiciel, de spécification logicielle, d'architecture et conception, de test des solutions (robustesse, performance, etc), de rédaction de publications (et participation à des conférences du domaine). Compétences scientifiques et techniques recherchées : Fondamentaux scientifiques (mathématique, statistique, probabilité, algèbre, optimisation numérique…) et techniques de développement logiciel (langages programmation C++, Python, algorithmie en général…) solides Deep Learning, réseaux de neurones, méthodes d’entrainement… Planification sous incertitude, Décision Séquentielle, Apprentissage par renforcement... IA Générative & LLM (Transformers, Prompt engineering, RAG, Fine-tuning, Agentique…) Industrialisation & MLOps (Hardware et Infrastructure, CI/CD, déploiement des modèles en production, Monitoring). Compétences relationnelles et non techniques recherchées : De curiosité scientifique et technique, pour le secteur défense en particulier. D’adaptation (au domaine de l’aéronautique et la simulation de vol, à la complexité du sujet, à la diversité des compétences requises). D’appétences pour les défis technologiques. De capacités d’abstraction du problème posé. De prise de recul et d’anticipation. D’autonomie et de proposition d’idées. D’aisance organisationnelle et relationnelle.

items.title: PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA"
items.desc: PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA" Réf ABG-140512 Sujet de Thèse 13/10/2026 Financement de l'Union européenne Sorbonne Université Lieu de travail Paris - Ile-de-France - France Intitulé du sujet PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA" Champs scientifiques Biologie Santé, médecine humaine, vétérinaire Mots clés Biological sciences, Biology, Medical sciences, Neurosciences, Immunology Description du sujet The position focuses on "Evaluating how complement dysregulation influences mononuclear phagocyte accumulation in AMD" within the MSCA Doctoral Network PANDORA (Discovering Pathomechanisms and Novel Drug Optimization for AMD). Subretinal mononuclear phagocytes (MPs) build up in the photoreceptor cell layer, a zone normally kept free of immune cells by the immunosuppressive retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). This build-up is a key driver of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). MPs include microglia and monocyte-derived inflammatory macrophages (MoMφ). Our team has shown that activated MPs evade RPE-mediated clearance. We have also shown that the AMD-linked CFH 402H variant impairs the removal of subretinal MPs independently of its role in the complement system. How complement dysregulation contributes to immune cell accumulation in the subretinal space in AMD remains poorly understood. The PhD student will first map where complement cascade components are found in the human retina. Using multiplexed immunohistochemistry on post-mortem retinal sections from AMD donors and age-matched controls, the student will localise components of the classical, lectin and alternative pathways, their activation products, regulators (CFH and Factor H-related proteins) and receptors. These components will be mapped relative to subretinal MPs, the RPE, photoreceptors and drusen. The student will then study how the Chromosome 1 (Chr1) AMD risk haplotype affects RPE, microglia and MoMφ and their interactions. They will use control and Chr1-risk iPSC-derived cells in a well-defined co-culture system developed in our laboratory. The student will also study the role of plasma-derived Factor H-related proteins (FHR1-5) using depleted human plasma and purified complement factors. Using single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing and proteomics, the student will analyse how complement dysregulation affects: microglia and MoMφ polarisation the interaction of these cells with the immunosuppressive RPE key inflammatory pathways and immune functions in the subretinal microenvironment, in health and in AMD Finally, the student will test whether complement inhibitors (anti-C5, anti-C3) can restore immune balance. The project is supervised by Dr. Florian Sennlaub (Institut de la Vision, Paris) It is carried out in close collaboration with other PANDORA doctoral candidates. Techniques and Training Include: Multiplexed immunohistochemistry on human donor retinal sections (AMD and age-matched controls), whole-slide/confocal imaging and quantitative image analysis Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived RPE, microglia and macrophage models, and immune cell/RPE co-cultures Primary human monocyte isolation and differentiation, and work with human plasma and purified complement factors Single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, and proteomics Flow cytometry, qPCR, western blot, ELISA/multiplex cytokine assays Functional immune assays (phagocytosis, migration, survival/clearance) Prise de fonction : 01/02/2027 Nature du financement Financement de l'Union européenne Précisions sur le financement Horizon Europe – MSCA (Marie Curie Actions) Présentation établissement et labo d'accueil Sorbonne Université Founded by Professor José-Alain Sahel, the Institut de la Vision is an international research centre dedicated entirely to research into eye and vision diseases. It brings together researchers, doctors, patients and industry on the same site to discover innovative treatments for eye diseases and improve the quality of life of visually impaired people. It is being built on a site that brings together l’Hôpital national de la vision des 15-20 and its Clinical Investigation Centre (CIC), as well as the Centre for Rare Retinal Diseases. Designed as a place where people can come together and exchange ideas, the Institut de la Vision enables ideas to be shared, new questions to emerge and the transfer of research findings to patient care to be accelerated. Its innovative organisation, based around hospital patients, enables new therapeutic or technological solutions to be discovered, tested and developed in order to prevent eye diseases or limit their effects. items.desc: Your job Have you ever wondered how we can ensure that climate mitigation and adaptation policies are fair, coherent, and effective? Are you interested in applying state-of-the-art impact evaluation techniques to analyze how climate policies affect land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity? Do you good communication skills in Spanish? Then this might be your next step! Climate change mitigation and adaptation in agriculture and forestry represent a “wicked problem”, shaped by uncertainty, conflicting objectives, institutional fragmentation and time pressure. While the EU has set ambitious climate targets for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, progress in agriculture and forestry remains insufficient and current policy frameworks have not yet resulted in significant climate mitigation and adaptation results, or generated the systemic transformation needed. This PhD position is part of the EU-Horizon project “ Evidence-based pathways towards fair, coherent and effective climate policies for Europe’s agriculture and forestry (PolicyForClimate) ”, which will develop tools and frameworks to enable policymakers and other stakeholders to design fair, coherent, and effective climate mitigation and adaptation policies in the EU. The project will use AI-assisted evidence synthesis, a policy-lab approach, and embedded case studies to offer a continuously updated evidence base on policy impacts, trade-offs, synergies, and spillovers. Your research will focus on developing, applying, and validating a novel mixed-methods framework for ex-post impact evaluation of climate policies in forestry and agricultural landscapes. By combining state-of-the-art econometric techniques with qualitative participatory approaches, you will empirically analyze how climate policies have affected land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity metrics. This will require conducting systematic reviews on existing impact evaluation frameworks, run workshops and focus group discussions with various stakeholders, collect, combine, and analyze farm-level primary data and secondary spatially explicit data. Start date: February 2027. Your duties and responsibilities include: Conduct systematic literature reviews and workshops to develop a mixed-methods ex-post impact evaluation framework for climate policies; Apply rigorous econometric methods together with qualitative assessments , particularly from policy sciences, to evaluate the impact of specific climate policies on land cover, carbon, and biodiversity metrics; Conduct focus group discussions with various stakeholders in the EU to validate the proposed impact evaluation framework and results from the empirical analyses; Write research papers and present research findings at international academic conferences; Collaborate with our research partners and contribute to the dissemination of project results . Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. items.desc: The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. You can read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Project description Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also computationally expensive. This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines. The qualification requirements must be fulfilled before admission to the programme. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements additionally require a minimum of 90 higher education credits in any of the fields of meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry; and at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics as well as a degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. At least 60 higher education credits of these courses must be on the second-cycle level. In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required. The specific entry requirements may also be fulfilled by a person who has otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. However, the fact that an applicant is deemed able to transfer credits from previous training or professional experience may not alone give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Admission decisions are made in accordance with current delegation policies. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. Project description Clouds regulate how much sunlight reaches the Earth’s surface and how much thermal radiation escapes to space, which ultimately influences how hot or cold the planet is. How much each cloud cools or warms the Earth depends in part on its composition. Is it made up of liquid particles, ice particles, or both? How densely spaced and how large are these particles? The answers to these questions lie partially in the dynamics occurring within the cloud. Even clouds that look calm from the ground may generate motions strong enough to shake an airplane. These motions can form new cloud particles and combine or shatter existing ones. However, these motions are difficult to represent completely in computer models of the atmosphere and in laboratory experiments, and we have yet to understand their full impact. The PhD student will build this understanding using over 800 hours of wind and cloud particle measurements that have been recorded by specialized research aircraft during field campaigns run by government agencies in the US and Europe. Data have been collected over the midwestern US and the Caribbean, off the northwestern coast of Africa, between Australia and Antarctica, and in the vicinity of Svalbard. Quality-controlled versions of all data are already available, so analysis can begin at the project start.The PhD student will develop a detailed understanding of aircraft instrumentation through literature review and apply that expertise to the analysis of measurements from dozens of different aircraft-mounted instruments. All analysis will be done in Python. The scientific scope initially spans micrometer-scale cloud particles to the dynamical processes that affect clouds, including turbulent eddies and kilometer-scale atmospheric waves. Initial science questions are well defined and focus on identifying statistical relationships between cloud particle properties and cloud-scale dynamics, and investigating how these vary across cloud types and geographic regions. After the initial stage, the project is more open-ended. The PhD student may choose to focus on the same micrometer–kilometer scales, or to make connections between these scales and the regional or global climate. They may also choose to branch into atmospheric modelling and/or to use machine learning to model observed relationships between cloud dynamics and cloud particles. items.desc: PhD student in Geophysics: Enhancing exploration drilling efficiency through integrated analyses rock formation and drilling data Are you interested in working with sustainable and responsible exploration drilling of critical raw materials, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University. The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden's most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues. Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development. Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland. In geophysics we use quantitative physical methods to investigate the Earth and its environment. In addition, physical property measurements, rock mechanical field testing, scientific drilling and numerical modelling are employed to investigate the subsurface structures and processes. The Geophysics program currently runs several national and international projects and has a wealth of world-class infrastructures. It also leads the Smart Exploration Research Center (SERC) (www.smartexploration.se). SERC is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, with members from four Swedish universities, three mining companies, four technology companies, and one development company. In this PhD project, you will be enrolled as a PhD student at Uppsala University in close collaboration with Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro. You will mainly be placed at Uppsala University, Uppsala. Access to certain technology or data associated with industry partners within the project may be subject to applicable export control legislation and will be managed in accordance with current regulations. Duties The PhD candidate will conduct research within SERC, focusing on sustainable and responsible exploration of critical raw materials. The overarching aim of the PhD project is to develop a framework for integrating rock formation and drilling data to improve exploration drilling efficiency, thereby contribute to more sustainable and responsible exploration drilling. The project combines geoscience and drilling technology, with a focus on diamond core drilling in crystalline rock. The PhD candidate will develop advanced theoretical, technical and practical expertise in the technical and operational challenges of the drilling process, as well as geoscientific methods for subsurface characterization. The work involves data acquisition in connection with exploration drilling, borehole logging, in-situ testing, drill core analyses, and laboratory testing. Separate and integrated analyses of these datasets will be used to investigate potential relationships between rock formation properties, drilling data, and exploration drilling efficiency. The doctoral student will work in close collaboration with academic and industry research groups contributing to stronger collaboration and knowledge exchange between these communities. The PhD candidate is expected to combine theoretical and practical work, work both independently and collaboratively, spend parts of the project period with industry partners, and participate in field and laboratory work. We are seeking a candidate with strong interests in exploration drilling in crystalline rocks and methods for subsurface characterisation, both in-situ and in the laboratory. Good oral and written proficiency in English is required. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively is considered a merit. Proficiency in spoken and written Swedish is a merit, because communication in Swedish may be required during fieldwork and collaboration with industry partners. A driving license is a merit, as it may be required for fieldwork. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns att läsa på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektet syftar till att öka förståelsen för hur aerosolföroreningar påverkar moln som består av vattendroppar. Inom projektet ges möjlighet att undersöka detta genom att testa en ny teori som förutspår att aerosolföroreningar förstärker uppvindarna i konvektiva moln, vilket kan göra molnen tjockare och mer reflekterande. Det finns även möjlighet att studera trender i jordens strålningsbudget kopplade till aerosol-moln-interaktioner under satelliteran. items.title: PhD position in biomineralization of digitally fabricated granular materials
items.desc: Mission We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student in the Laloui Group at EPFL inLausanne. The group brings expertise in geomaterials and their mechanical behaviour to research at theinterface of material science and engineering applications. You will work on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital FabricationUsing Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration between Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the LalouiGroup at EPFL, and co-PI Prof. Benjamin Dillenburger of the Chair of Digital Building Technologies at ETHZurich. The project investigates how biologically driven mineralization can transform demolition and excavationmaterials into materials suitable for digital fabrication under ambient conditions. Digital fabrication methods, including extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying, offer opportunities to controlmaterial placement and curing, create complex geometries and reduce material consumption. Integratingbiomineralization into pumpable, extrudable and sprayable granular materials remains largely unexplored. ThisPhD will investigate the coupled biogeochemical, rheological and mechanical mechanisms governing particledeposition, mineral precipitation and hardening. Main duties and responsibilities As a PhD Student, you will be expected to: Take full responsibility for your dissertation and the progress of your research. Conduct research in close collaboration with project partners at EPFL and ETH Zurich and, whereapplicable, industry partners. Design and execute experiments, and analyze and interpret experimental results. Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present your findings at internationalconferences. Participate in teaching and supervise student projects. More specifically, within this project, you will: Investigate the rheology and processability of granular materials, including yield stress, plastic viscosity,thixotropy, water content, ageing and particle interactions. Study microbial activity and biologically driven mineral precipitation, and determine how evolving mineralphases affect mechanical hardening and material performance. Characterize the coupling between biogeochemical reactions, rheological properties and mechanicalbehaviour over space and time. Connect experimental findings to extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying in collaboration with thedigital fabrication team at ETH Zurich. items.title: SNSF-funded PhD position in lipid metabolism
items.desc: Dysregulation of lipid metabolism plays a key role in development and progression of metabolic disorders including obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). items.title: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time. The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data. The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project. Responsibilities Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data. Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction. Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits. Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities. Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging. Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects. Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations. Qualifications You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English. To succeed in this position, you are expected to have: A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models. Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks. A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations. Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion. Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning. Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling. Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction. Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation. At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Hans Martin Kjer, hmkj@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 16 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Compute DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk . DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: Doctorante / Doctorant CIFRE Fiabilité des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire
items.desc: Description De L'employeur Le Groupe SNCF a pour vocation de simplifier les déplacements, fluidifier le transport des personnes et des marchandises, et développer la mobilité de demain. Au sein du Groupe SNCF, la Direction Technologies, Innovation et Projets Groupe (DTIPG) est une direction de la SA SNCF chargée de l'innovation technologique appliquée aux projets stratégiques du groupe. Elle contribue notamment à concevoir un système ferroviaire plus fiable, numérique et décarboné, avec des travaux sur l'IA, les nouvelles propulsions et la localisation des trains. Dans ce cadre, le pôle RECHERCHE - DIRECTION SCIENTIFIQUE propose un projet de thèse CIFRE sur la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire , en partenariat avec le Laboratoire en Génie Industriel (LGI) de CentraleSupélec au sein de la chaire Risques et Résilience des Systèmes Complexes (RRSC) . Description Du Poste La doctorante ou le doctorant CIFRE aura pour mission de développer une méthode d'évaluation et de communication de la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques (JN) appliqués aux systèmes ferroviaires. Les principales activités seront : Comprendre et formaliser les usages des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire : Analyse des cas d'usage SNCF et partenaires (conception numérique, supervision du patrimoine, planification de la maintenance, régénération du réseau). Cartographie des composants d'un JN (données, modèles sous-jacents, processus, interfaces). Réaliser un état de l'art approfondi : Revue bibliographique sur les concepts de jumeaux numériques, la qualité des données et des modèles, la confiance et la fiabilité perçue par les utilisateurs. Analyse des normes et référentiels (notamment ISO/IEC 30173:2023 et ISO 23247:2021) et des modèles de maturité (Digital Twin Business Maturity Model). Cartographier et classifier les cas d'usage SNCF : Identification des étapes de conception d'un JN et de ses niveaux de maturité. Recueil des usages métiers (par qui, pour quoi) et des limites identifiées. Analyse de la fiabilité perçue : critères utilisés, justifications, attentes des utilisateurs. Méthodes : entretiens, analyse documentaire, enquêtes auprès des équipes SNCF et des partenaires. Étudier en profondeur un ou plusieurs cas d'étude : Définition du processus complet de conception et d'utilisation d'un JN sur un cas choisi (par exemple un système de signalisation ou un sous-système d'infrastructure). Identification des étapes où interviennent les contraintes de fiabilité (collecte des données, modélisation, prédiction, décision). Modélisation du processus de conception et d'usage du JN. Méthodes : entretiens, analyse de données, modélisation de processus. Proposer une méthode de notation de la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques : Analyse des enjeux : pour qui, pourquoi et à quoi sert la notation (support à la décision, communication, gouvernance). Définition des dimensions d'évaluation de la fiabilité, éventuellement différenciées selon les types de JN (descriptif, diagnostique, prédictif, prescriptif, autonome). Choix et formalisation d'une méthodologie de notation (par exemple analyse multicritère, indicateurs composites inspirés de modèles type « nutri-score » adaptés aux JN). Expérimentation et test de la méthode sur un ou plusieurs cas d'étude ferroviaire. Conception participative avec des experts métiers et techniques SNCF. Inscrire les travaux dans un écosystème européen : Veille et participation aux travaux autour des jumeaux numériques ferroviaires dans le projet Motional du programme Europes'Rail, et le cas échéant Motional 2. Valorisation des résultats de la thèse auprès des partenaires européens (présentations, publications, contributions aux groupes de travail). Production scientifique et valorisation : Rédaction d'articles scientifiques, rapports internes SNCF, supports de vulgarisation pour les métiers. Participation à des conférences et séminaires (académiques et industriels). Profil recherché Diplômé(e) de Master 2 ou école d'ingénieur Dans Un Des Domaines Suivants (ou Apparentés) Génie industriel Modélisation et simulation de systèmes complexes Ingénierie des systèmes Mathématiques appliquées / data science avec forte appétence pour les systèmes industriels Ou formation équivalente avec solide bagage en modélisation et analyse de systèmes. Un intérêt marqué pour le système ferroviaire , ses enjeux techniques et humains, est attendu. Compétences techniques Solide maîtrise de la modélisation et de la simulation de systèmes complexes (approches systèmes, modèles de processus, éventuellement outils de modélisation type UML, SysML ou équivalents). Connaissances en ingénierie des systèmes et/ou génie industriel. Capacité à mener un état de l'art scientifique : recherche bibliographique, analyse critique d'articles, synthèse. Aisance avec les méthodes d'analyse multicritère et d'évaluation (indicateurs, agrégation, notation). Compétences en analyse de données et compréhension des enjeux de qualité des données (détection d'anomalies, données aberrantes, capteurs IoT...). Excellentes capacités de rédaction en français et en anglais (articles, rapports, documents méthodologiques). Compétences comportementales Capacité d'écoute et de dialogue avec des interlocuteurs variés (experts techniques, chercheurs, opérationnels métiers). Rigueur scientifique, sens de l'analyse et de la synthèse. Très bon relationnel et aptitude à travailler en interface entre monde académique et industriel. Autonomie, curiosité, goût pour l'innovation et la transformation numérique. Capacité à vulgariser des concepts complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux décideurs et aux utilisateurs métiers. Ce que le contrat CIFRE vous apportera Une expérience de recherche appliquée au coeur des enjeux de transformation numérique du ferroviaire : vous travaillerez sur un sujet stratégique pour SNCF et ses partenaires, à l'interface entre innovation digitale, systèmes complexes et performance du réseau. Une double immersion académique et industrielle : Au LGI de CentraleSupélec, au sein de la chaire RRSC, dans un environnement scientifique de haut niveau. Au sein de SNCF Holding - Direction Technologies, Innovation & Projets Groupe, en lien direct avec des experts du jumeau numérique, de la donnée et des systèmes ferroviaires. Un sujet fortement valorisable : Production d'une méthode de référence pour évaluer la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques ferroviaires. Contributions possibles à des projets européens (Motional, Europes'Rail) et à des groupes de normalisation ou de standardisation. Des perspectives professionnelles solides : Expertise rare et recherchée sur les jumeaux numériques, la fiabilité et la confiance dans les systèmes digitaux. Profil attractif pour le secteur ferroviaire, la mobilité, l'industrie et la tech (ingénierie systèmes, data, R&D, innovation). items.title: Doktorand i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi, med fokus på ML-metoder i klimatmodellering
items.desc: Meteorologiska institutionen vid Stockholms universitet (MISU) bedriver forskning och utbildning som rör atmosfären, oceanen, och fysikaliskt-baserad klimatvetenskap. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektbeskrivning Moln och deras förändringar till följd av variationer i omgivande miljö spelar en avgörande för klimat och klimatförändringar. Upplösningen i typiska klimatmodeller är dock alldeles för grov för att de ska kunna representera processer relaterade till molnbildning explicit. Dessa processer behöver därför parametriseras, eller representeras som funktioner av storskaliga tillståndsvariabler. Sådana parametriseringar är behäftade med stor osäkerhet, och dessutom är de beräkningsmässigt kostsamma. Det här projektets fokus är att på nya sätt brygga över mellan mikroskala och global skala, för att förbättra klimatmodellers noggrannhet, effektivitet och generaliserbarhet och samtidigt utnyttja modern beräkningshårdvara. Vi kommer att undersöka hur maskininlärningsmodeller (ML-modeller) kan tränas på observationer och resultat från högupplöst modellering, som alternativ till empiriska parmetriseringar av småskaliga processer relaterade till turbulens, molnbildning och aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Specifikt ingår i uppgifterna att utveckla och träna datadrivna modeller, koppla dem till en storskalig klimatmodell, utvärdera resultaten mot mätningar och traditionellt parametriserade modeller, och att använda den ML-förstärkta modellen till att uppskatta klimatrelevans som molns effekt på strålningsbalansen, och strålningsdrivning från aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Arbetet kommer att utföras i nära samarbete med experter inom datavetenskap, inom Swedish e-Science Research Centre, och bidra till metodutveckling med bredare tillämpning än endast klimatvetenskap. Som doktorand i projektet kommer du att utveckla dina färdigheter inom atmosfärsvetenskap och klimatmodellering, men även inom datavetenskap och maskininlärning, samt kommunikation och samarbete inom och mellan discipliner. Behörighetskrav För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning krävs att den sökande har grundläggande och särskild behörighet. Behörigheten ska vara uppfylld senast vid antagning till programmet. Grundläggande behörighet har du, om du avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng (hp), varav minst 60 hp på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. För särskild behörighet krävs minst 90 hp i något av ämnena meteorologi, oceanografi, fysik eller kemi, minst 15 hp i matematik och ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 hp. Av detta skall minst 60 hp vara på avancerad nivå. Vidare krävs språkkunskaper i engelska motsvarande engelska B på gymnasiet. Vid bedömningen tas hänsyn till förtrogenhet och skicklighet inom ämnet, förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska, analytisk förmåga, kreativitet, initiativförmåga och självständighet, och samarbetsförmåga. Till grund för bedömningen ligger tidigare studiers relevans, betyg på genomgångna högskolekurser (särskilt de på avancerad nivå), kvalitet och omfattning på det självständiga arbetet, referenser, intervjuer samt skriftlig avsiktsförklaring. items.title: Offre de thèse CIFRE Janvier/Février 2027
items.desc: Pérennisation soutenable des systèmes de production : modélisation probabiliste hybride et anticipation des risques d’obsolescence Contexte et problématique Une part importante de l’outil industriel repose aujourd’hui sur des installations exploitées depuis plusieurs décennies. Ces moyens de production associent des équipements, composants, automatismes et logiciels dont la durée d’exploitation dépasse fréquemment celle de commercialisation ou de support. L’obsolescence constitue ainsi un risque important pour la continuité de production. Elle peut résulter d’évolutions technologiques, de l’arrêt d’une référence, de la raréfaction de pièces, de la disparition d’un fournisseur, de la fin d’un support ou de la perte de compétences. Sa maîtrise constitue un enjeu de disponibilité des installations, de souveraineté industrielle et d’utilisation raisonnée des ressources. Une installation industrielle comporte plusieurs milliers de références reliées entre elles au sein d’architectures techniques et de chaînes d’approvisionnement complexes. Les informations nécessaires à l’évaluation de leur pérennité sont dispersées entre bases de maintenance, référentiels techniques, données fournisseurs, historiques d’intervention et connaissances métier. Ces informations sont hétérogènes, évolutives et souvent incomplètes. Le module de diagnostic du logiciel OBSOLIO, développé par GreenTrack Genius, évalue actuellement l’obsolescence au moyen d’un scoring expert statique. La thèse vise à dépasser cette approche pour construire un modèle capable d’actualiser et d’anticiper le risque d’obsolescence à partir des données disponibles et des connaissances métier, tout en représentant explicitement l’incertitude et les mécanismes de propagation du risque. Question scientifique centrale Comment modéliser, propager et actualiser le risque d’obsolescence au sein d’une architecture industrielle multiniveau et de sa chaîne d’approvisionnement, en présence d’informations hétérogènes et incomplètes, afin de comparer de manière explicable des stratégies de pérennisation soutenable ? Verrou scientifique et approche proposée Le principal verrou scientifique concerne la propagation probabiliste d’un risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau, depuis le composant jusqu’à l’équipement et à la ligne de production, alors que l’état de connaissance sur les différents éléments du système est incomplet et variable. Une absence d’information sur une référence, un fournisseur ou une possibilité de substitution ne peut en effet être assimilée à l’absence de risque, ni être systématiquement considérée comme une situation défavorable. La modélisation devra donc distinguer autant que possible le risque déduit des informations disponibles de l’incertitude liée à l’incomplétude de ces informations. La recherche s’appuiera sur une approche hybride associant deux niveaux de représentation. 1. Représentation des connaissances et de l’architecture industrielle Un graphe de connaissances sera utilisé pour structurer les relations entre actifs, composants, nomenclatures, fournisseurs, références de substitution, historiques et événements d’obsolescence. Ce graphe aura pour fonction de représenter la structure du système étudié et les informations disponibles. Une question de recherche portera sur la manière de transformer ou d’exploiter cette représentation pour construire les dépendances pertinentes du modèle probabiliste. 2. Modélisation et propagation probabilistes Les réseaux bayésiens constitueront le cadre principal étudié pour agréger les connaissances expertes et les observations disponibles, représenter les dépendances entre facteurs et propager l’incertitude entre les différents niveaux du système. La dimension temporelle sera introduite lorsque les données disponibles permettent de caractériser l’évolution des variables et du risque. Les extensions dynamiques des réseaux bayésiens seront notamment étudiées pour représenter cette évolution et évaluer leur capacité à anticiper une situation d’obsolescence. Le travail portera en particulier sur les méthodes d’initialisation du modèle, l’intégration de connaissances expertes, l’apprentissage à partir des historiques et la robustesse de l’inférence en présence de données manquantes. Aide à la décision et pérennisation soutenable L’objectif est de dépasser le diagnostic pour comparer des stratégies de remédiation. Les réseaux bayésiens pourront être étendus sous forme de diagrammes d’influence, intégrant variables de décision et critères d’utilité. Plusieurs stratégies seront considérées : maintien en l’état, constitution ou mutualisation de stocks, substitution, reconditionnement, reconception partielle ou renouvellement. La pérennisation soutenable sera abordée comme un problème de décision multicritère prenant en compte au minimum : la disponibilité et le risque technique ; le coût de la stratégie ; son impact environnemental ; sa faisabilité industrielle et organisationnelle. L’objectif sera donc d’identifier la solution réduisant le risque d’obsolescence mais aussi de comparer les conséquences de différentes stratégies dans le contexte propre au système étudié. Validation et résultats attendus La validation reposera sur des données industrielles historiques : données de maintenance et d’équipements, informations fournisseurs, changements de références, événements d’obsolescence et autres données de cycle de vie disponibles sur les sites étudiés. Une validation rétrospective sera privilégiée. Elle consistera, lorsque les données le permettent, à reconstruire l’état d’information disponible à une date passée, à produire l’évaluation du risque correspondant, puis à comparer cette évaluation aux événements observés ultérieurement. Les résultats seront également comparés au scoring expert actuellement utilisé dans OBSOLIO afin de mesurer l’apport de la modélisation probabiliste en matière d’anticipation, de gestion des données manquantes et d’explicabilité. La thèse devra aboutir à trois résultats principaux : un modèle formel de représentation et de propagation probabiliste du risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau ; une méthode d’aide à la décision permettant de comparer des stratégies de pérennisation selon plusieurs critères ; un démonstrateur Python mettant en œuvre les modèles développés et permettant leur validation sur des cas industriels. Les contributions scientifiques porteront ainsi sur la représentation et la propagation d’un risque d’obsolescence dans des systèmes industriels complexes lorsque l’information disponible est distribuée, évolutive et incomplète. Les résultats auront vocation à alimenter le moteur algorithmique d’OBSOLIO, sans que le développement du logiciel constitue l’objet de la thèse. Profil recherché Le ou la candidate devra être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master en génie industriel, ingénierie des systèmes, science des données, informatique industrielle ou domaine proche. De solides bases en probabilités, statistiques et modélisation sont attendues, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de la programmation scientifique en Python. Une connaissance des réseaux bayésiens, des modèles graphiques probabilistes ou des méthodes de recherche opérationnelle constituera un atout. Le travail nécessitera également une capacité à comprendre des architectures industrielles complexes et à travailler avec les équipes de maintenance, méthodes, achats et ingénierie. Le profil recherché doit ainsi associer compétences en modélisation et intérêt pour les problématiques industrielles concrètes. Contact : Marc.Zolghadri@isae-supmeca.fr
